column1: # OpenSubtitles 2018 English word frequencies, 50,000 types, rank order.
#         fetched 2026-08-11, md5 370a7a55f79605b25638e3e262d5f920 of the upstream file
# LICENCE MIT (LICENSE at the repo root, "Copyright (c) 2016 Hermit Dave")
#         over OpenSubtitles 2018 as distributed by OPUS.
# WHY IT IS HERE. It is the REGISTER replacement for wordfreq20k.txt, which is
# a 2006 web crawl (see that file's row in data/sources.tsv). Spoken English
# inverts the web list's pathology: `moon` outranks `yahoo` by 13.7x here,
# where the web list has `yahoo` outranking `moon` by 5.6x, and `weep`, `wept`
# and `mourn` exist at all -- the web list has none of the three, which in
# `lyric_harness.CandidateEngine` means not merely unranked but UNOFFERABLE.
# WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX. It is still a GLOBAL UNIGRAM RANK. Measured
# leave-one-author-out against what 69 held-out authors actually reached for,
# it blocks 21.4% of realised rhyme partners against the web list's 16.9% --
# real, and small beside the 63.2% the line-final CONDITIONAL reaches. The
# head of any unigram list is function words, and inside a rhyme field that is
# where the exclusion gets spent. quality/RESULTS_SONG_FREQUENCY.md.
# TOKENISATION. Upstream splits clitics, so `'s` and `'t` are types (ranks 6
# and 10). They are kept as they came rather than silently merged: a count is
# a coordinate of its tokenisation (doctrine 58/91) and the next person to
# measure this should see the same file the number came from.
# INDEPENDENT of every corpus in this repo -- contemporary film and television
# subtitles are not verse, are not sung, and are not any cell's labelled pool.
